name: AlgMap-11.5
questiontext:
Rearrange \({{CT:0}} = {{CT:1}}\) and make \(a\) the subject of the formula.

\(a\) = [[input:ans]] [[validation:ans]]
generalfeedback:
To rearrange formulae perform operations to both sides of the formulae to obtain an equation with \(a\) as the subject.
\[ {{CT:0}} = {{CT:1}}. \]
The aim is to get \(a\) on the opposite side of the equation to the other constants/variables. In order to do this it is clear we must 'free' the \(a\) from the brackets. We do this by multiplying out \({{CT:1}}\) which gives:
\[ {{CT:0}} = {{CT:2}}. \]
Subtract \({{CT:3}}\) from both sides:
\[ {{CT:4}} = {{CT:5}}. \]
Divide by \({{CT:6}}\):
\[ {{CT:7}} = {{CT:8}}. \]
You now have an equation for \(a\).
